newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Ruling ODS ahead in early Czech Senate results.
newsitem.headline: Ruling ODS ahead in early Czech Senate results.

text.p: Early results from Czech Senate elections on Saturday showed that the ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS) of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus had gained most votes in the three constituencies declared so far.

But figures released by the Central Election Commission showed that none of the three ODS candidates had won the required majority of the vote, and therefore have to contest a runoff on November 22-23 with the runner up.
But turnout in the three constituencies was dismally low, ranging from 26.36 percent in the northern mining town of Most to 29.78 in one constituency in the industrial city of Ostrava.
The ODS scored highest in Ostrava where its candidate took 41.04 percent to 24.85 percent for the Social Democrats, who were runners up in two of the three constituencies.
Runner up in Most was trade union leader Richard Falbr who is running as an independent but with Social Democrat backing.

Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec, an ODS vice chairman, cautiously welcomed the results. "I'm very happy that several of our candidates have moved into the next round, but the strength of the other candidates in the second round will be high and it will be immensely demanding," he told reporters.
